summary: Specifies an extension to RTCP that lets receivers use unicast feedback to a multicast sender. It is useful for single-source multicast such as Source-Specific Multicast, where the traditional many-to-many feedback model does not fit. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5760 lets receivers in a one-source multicast session send RTCP reports directly to a Feedback Target by unicast. The Distribution Source can repeat each report to the group or send a summary of the reports.

subtitle: How RTCP receivers can report to a multicast source using unicast, with optional report summaries.

tldr.problem: In one-to-many multicast, receivers may not be able to send RTCP to the whole group. Building a many-to-many multicast network just for feedback may also be unnecessary.
tldr.mechanism: Receivers send RTCP reports by unicast to a Feedback Target. The Distribution Source either reflects each report to the group or consolidates reports into Receiver Summary Information packets.
tldr.outcome: The extension supports RTCP feedback for single-source multicast without changing the RTP data stream. RFC 5760 is updated by RFC 6128.

today: RFC 5760 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2010 and is updated by RFC 6128.

sections.title: Why Receivers Need a Return Channel
sections.content:
RTP carries real-time media, while the RTP Control Protocol (RTCP) carries reports about matters such as packet loss and round-trip time. In a source-specific multicast (SSM) session, media flows from the source to receivers, but receivers may not be able to send multicast traffic back to the group.

RFC 5760 adds unicast feedback: each receiver sends RTCP to a Feedback Target, and the Distribution Source shares the resulting feedback with the group. The RTP data stream itself is unchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: Receivers in some multicast sessions cannot send control reports back to the whole group. This RFC lets them send those reports by unicast to a designated target.

sections.title: The Participants and Feedback Models
sections.content:
The Distribution Source sends RTP data to receivers and redistributes RTCP information. A Media Sender originates RTP packets. The Feedback Target is the address or logical function that receives unicast RTCP from receivers; it may be part of the Distribution Source or a separate entity.

The Simple Feedback Model reflects each receiver's RTCP packet individually. The Distribution Source Feedback Summary Model aggregates information and distributes summaries. The session description selects the model before the session begins, and the Distribution Source must not change it during the session.
sections.plainLanguage: Receivers send reports to a Feedback Target, and the Distribution Source returns information to the group. It either repeats individual reports or sends summaries.

sections.title: Simple Feedback: Reflecting Reports
sections.content:
The Simple Feedback Model uses the usual RTCP packet types. The Distribution Source listens for unicast RTCP and forwards each valid receiver packet to the multicast RTCP channel. It must not combine report blocks from different receivers into one reflected packet.

Receivers continue to send Receiver Reports and follow RTCP bandwidth rules. The Distribution Source also forwards sender RTCP to receivers and, when needed, relays receiver reports to Media Senders. This model requires little change to existing receiver behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: In the simple model, the Distribution Source repeats each valid receiver report to the group without combining reports from different receivers.

sections.title: Summary Reports and the RSI Packet
sections.content:
The summary model adds a Receiver Summary Information (RSI) RTCP packet with payload type 209. Its fixed fields identify the Distribution Source, the summarized Media Sender, and the report timestamp. Optional sub-report blocks can describe distributions of loss, jitter, round-trip time, or cumulative loss, or carry a Feedback Target address and group information.

Distribution blocks use a 12-bit bucket count and a 4-bit multiplicative-factor field. Each RSI must include either a group-and-average-packet-size report or an RTCP bandwidth report so receivers can calculate their reporting interval.
sections.plainLanguage: The RSI packet identifies the source and carries a timestamp. Optional blocks summarize receiver reports or tell receivers how much RTCP bandwidth they may use.

sections.title: Session Signaling and Security
sections.content:
SDP uses the rtcp-unicast attribute to identify the feedback method. The value reflection selects the Simple Feedback Model; rsi selects the summary model. SDP also identifies the Distribution Source and can specify an alternative Feedback Target.

A forged or incorrect Feedback Target address can direct traffic from many receivers to another host. Source traffic must have integrity and source authentication; protection for receiver feedback is recommended. A mistakenly configured address can still cause unwanted traffic even when it came from an authenticated source. RFC 5760 is updated by RFC 6128.
sections.plainLanguage: SDP tells participants whether reports will be reflected or summarized. A wrong Feedback Target can attract traffic from many receivers, so the address and source information need protection.
